[[File:Eric Berger Ars Technica.jpg|thumb|right|260px|Eric Berger. Photo: Ars Technica.]]
'''Eric Berger''' won the 1997 Texas regional at Texas A&M University, 8–0, and played the [[1997 Decipher World Championship]] in Norfolk, Virginia, where he won one game of six.<ref name="ars">[https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2015/12/that-one-time-i-played-in-the-star-wars-card-game-world-championship/ That one time I played in the Star Wars card game world championship], Eric Berger, Ars Technica (5 December 2015). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009010838/https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2015/12/that-one-time-i-played-in-the-star-wars-card-game-world-championship/ Internet Archive]</ref> He began with Decipher's Star Trek CCG in 1995 alongside [[Brian Guthrie]] and stopped playing after Decipher lost the Star Wars license in 2001. In 2015 he wrote about his Worlds trip for Ars Technica and held a sealed-deck mini tournament with [[Mike Patterson]] and Tom Hoge.<ref name="ars" />
